units.title: Surgical Anatomy and Applied Renal Relationships
units.sec: Surgical Anatomy and Applied Renal Relationships · p327
units.guide: The kidney begins from metanephric buds in the iliac fossa and ascends to the lumbar region. Surgical relationships are high yield: the long left renal vein is the preferred donor side, its compression between SMA and aorta causes nutcracker syndrome, and the renal hilum reads posterior pelvis, middle artery, anterior vein.

units.title: Renal Agenesis and Duplication of the Ureteric System
units.sec: Renal Agenesis and Duplication of the Ureteric System · p328
units.guide: Renal agenesis is usually unilateral and travels with ipsilateral ureter/hemitrigone absence plus sex-specific genital anomalies. In a duplicated system, apply Weigert–Meyer: the upper-pole ureter ends distally and medially, producing ectopic drainage and the wet child, while IVU shows the drooping lily sign and symptomatic ectopic ureter is reimplanted.

units.title: Polycystic Kidney Disease
units.guide: Contrast infantile AR PKHD1-on-6 disease, often lethal from hepatic fibrosis, with adult AD PKD1-on-16/PKD2-on-4 disease. Enlarging cysts compress renal tissue and cause young hypertension, pain, haematuria and renal failure; liver cysts, berry aneurysm, diverticulosis and mitral prolapse are the extra-renal map, while advanced disease may need vasopressin antagonists, mTOR inhibition, dialysis or transplant.

units.title: Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney and Horseshoe Kidney
units.sec: Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney and Horseshoe Kidney · p330
units.guide: Multicystic dysplastic kidney can be unilateral or lethal when bilateral. Horseshoe kidney is a fused lower-pole kidney held below the inferior mesenteric artery: it may be asymptomatic but brings stones, infection and hydronephrosis; IVU gives a flower-vase/handshake sign, pyeloplasty relieves obstruction, and the isthmus is not divided except for a symptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm.

units.title: Hydronephrosis and PUJ Obstruction
units.guide: Hydronephrosis is aseptic pelvicalyceal dilation from intraluminal, intramural or extraluminal obstruction. Renal stones are the common acquired intraluminal cause, PUJ obstruction the common congenital intramural cause, and Anderson–Hynes treats symptomatic PUJ obstruction. Remember every named clue: goblet, cobra/adder head, maiden waist and the obstruction-specific repairs.

units.title: Retrocaval Ureter and Renal Isotope Scans
units.sec: Retrocaval Ureter and Renal Isotope Scans · p333
units.guide: A right retrocaval ureter lies behind the IVC and creates a fish-hook/reverse-J outline; lateralization and a DJ stent restore patency. MAG-3 best assesses function, DMSA shows scars and structure, and differential contribution below 10% marks a non-functioning kidney for nephrectomy while a contribution above 10% is saved.

units.title: Renal Stone Types and Composition
units.sec: Renal Stone Types and Composition · p334
units.guide: Citrate inhibits stones; calcium oxalate is common, acidic and radiopaque, struvite is alkaline Proteus-driven staghorn, cystine is hard and hexagonal in cystinuria, and uric acid is the common radiolucent stone linked to tumour lysis. Keep the crystal shapes, dietary measures and recurrent-stone drugs tied to their stone type.

units.title: Renal Stone Presentation and Investigation
units.sec: Renal Stone Presentation and Investigation · p335
units.guide: Stone pain follows anatomy: renal pelvis loin-to-groin, upper/mid ureter along iliohypogastric/obturator pathways, lower ureter along ilioinguinal pathway, and intramural impaction causes strangury. Dietl's crisis ends in a gush of dilute urine; NCCT KUB is the investigation of choice.

units.title: Management of Renal Stones
units.guide: Use the size algorithm without shortcuts: under 5 mm observe; symptomatic 5–6 mm gets tamsulosin and then ESWL if medical therapy fails. ESWL uses blast-wave ultrasound but is avoided in pregnancy, bleeding disorders, obesity, pacemakers, children, large/hard/lower-calyx stones and obstruction; RIRS handles smaller lower-pole stones and PCNL handles large, staghorn, hydronephrotic or previously failed cases.

units.title: Ureteric and Bladder Stones
units.guide: NCCT confirms ureteric and bladder stones. Remove ureteric stones over 5 mm ureteroscopically with a Dormia basket; primary bladder stones are sterile, paediatric mixed urate stones, while secondary adult stones follow infection/obstruction and are often calcium oxalate Jack stones. Perurethral cystolithotomy is first line unless urethral stricture or diverticulum calls for suprapubic cystolithotomy.
